problem: On ALFRED long-horizon mobile manipulation, end-to-end agents forget visited areas and re-explore, modular methods lift 2D semantics into 3D with imperfect depth and accumulate errors, and rigid hand-crafted execution cannot interrupt navigation to seize closer targets.
motivation: Long-horizon household tasks need persistent, spatially consistent memory and flexible execution to stay efficient. Depth-based back-projection accumulates errors over long episodes, and following fixed long-range plans wastes steps when a target appears earlier than expected.
key_idea: Build a depth-free persistent BEV-style 3D episodic memory via spatio-temporal deformable cross-attention, ground interaction masks by querying the image with memory-derived object features, and execute with a global BFS planner that a learned reactive local monitor can preempt.
insight: Temporal memory is the most important piece: removing MRU drops unseen SR from 61.27 to 27.16, versus 52.74 without OME. The reactive monitor mainly buys efficiency: removing AEP lowers unseen SR by 4.14 points and the efficiency factor PLWSR/SR falls (0.710 to 0.668 seen). Masks derived from memory are near GT-mask performance (unseen SR 61.27 vs 63.82), so grounding is not the bottleneck; language errors (~18-19% of episodes) are the main remaining failure.
method: Spatio-Temporal Fusion Mapping: a 100x100 grid (25 cm cells, C=256) of learnable BEV queries is autoregressively updated from a single egocentric RGB camera, giving a persistent 3D semantic map.

Observation-to-Memory Encoding (OME): lifts each grid query into pillar reference points, projects them into the current frame with the camera matrix, and aggregates ResNet50 features via deformable attention, so no depth estimation is needed.
Memory Retrieval and Update (MRU): temporal deformable cross-attention over the previous memory M_{t-1} plus spatial attention among neighbouring queries, preventing forgetting.
Semantic map head: predicts multi-hot categories (87 classes) per grid cell with BCE loss L_map.

Memory-Driven Target Grounding: mask-pools memory features over cells of the target class, applies an MLP to get a 3D object query, and takes its similarity with conv-mapped 2D image features to produce interaction masks; trained jointly with L = L_map + λ L_img.

Adaptive Execution Policy: random exploration over the navigable map until the target is detected, then a rule-based BFS global planner to the highest-probability target grid; a ResNet50 reactive local monitor predicts per-category manipulability and preempts the plan for immediate interaction, with a hierarchical fallback.
ALFRED pipeline: uses FILM's BERT language module to produce subgoal templates, with an initial 4x90° panoramic scan.

setting.backbone: ResNet50 + deformable-attention memory modules, trained from scratch on ALFRED; BERT language parser from FILM; rule-based BFS planner
setting.training_data: ALFRED expert trajectories (images, semantic maps, labels, following DISCO); the local monitor uses 332,432 images labelled by an expert planner with full scene knowledge
setting.observation: egocentric 300x300 RGB (60° FoV), agent pose from accumulated discrete actions
setting.action_space: ALFRED discrete: MoveAhead, Rotate L/R, LookUp/Down, 7 interaction actions (with masks), STOP
setting.privileged: none at test time (GT masks used only in an ablation)

results: ESCAPE reaches SOTA on ALFRED test with step-by-step instructions (SR 65.09 seen / 60.79 unseen), beating ThinkBot by 2.40 / 2.97 points. Without step-by-step instructions it reaches 61.24 / 56.04, beating DISCO by 3.24 / 1.34 points. Its PLWSR/PLWGC gains are large (e.g. unseen PLWSR 46.82 vs DISCO 36.50).
limitations: Language understanding is the largest failure source (~18-19% of episodes) and relies on the FILM BERT parser
Navigation collisions are higher in unseen scenes (11.57% vs 6.46%)
Evaluated only on ALFRED in simulation with a fixed 25m x 25m grid and 87 categories; the global planner is rule-based and there are no real-robot experiments
